Batteries degrade unevenly: one weak block in a string limits the autonomy of the whole system. Testing with the Fluke VT521 analyser measures the internal resistance and voltage of every block and detects such blocks before they fail. A controlled discharge shows the real autonomy of the system at the design load.

Batteries remain the most vulnerable part of a UPS: at 20–25 °C AGM batteries last 3–5 years (standard) or 10–12 years (long-life); at 30 °C the life is halved. Signs that replacement is needed: a battery error on the display, reduced autonomy, swollen cases, a voltage spread between blocks of more than 0.2 V.

Correct selection starts with the load: not the nameplate power of the equipment but the real consumption taking into account the power factor and inrush currents. Next the autonomy is determined: with a generator 10–15 minutes is enough, without one 30–60. Then the scheme is chosen: a monolithic UPS for simple tasks, modular for growth and redundancy, a parallel system for critical sites.
